description: Kondō Isami (16 years old) adopted by Shūsuke as heir to the Tennen Rishin sword fighting school
Bunkyū Era begins on this day
Hijikata Toshizō and a cohort of recruits form the Rōshi Corps and march from Edo
the Rōshi Corps arrives in Kyoto
Shikanai Kaoru meets Kotsuru in the woods outside of Chōrakuji temple
Kondō purchases the "Kotetsu" sword
recruits from Edo meet each other at Dentsū temple
Kiyokawa Hachirō assassinated at the Akabane Bridge in Kyoto
Tani Sanjūrō arrives at headquarters and is quickly promoted to the rank of Corporal
Meiji Era begins
Hijikata first suspects Okita has TB
Shinsengumi officially inaugurated
Hamaguri Gate Incident
Serizawa incident with Sumo wrestlers
assassination of Serizawa
Serizawa's funeral; Kondō takes full control of the corps
Fukamachi Shinsaku's first kill
Takeda and Yamazaki Susumu join Shinsengumi
Yamazaki returns to his dojo in Osaka to offer New Year's greetings to his master after having joined the Shinsengumi.
Yamazaki reports Masuya to Shinsengumi Fukamachi Shinsaku killed and discovery of the note leading to Ikedaya raid
Ikedaya Incident, chp 4 & chp 8; organizational structure redrawn, corporal becomes sergent;
Chōshū sympathizers forced out of Kyoto back to Choshu, overturning Choshu's powerful position in the capital
Itō Kashitarō leads a group of followers, including Shinohara Tainoshin, from his dojo in Edo to join the Shinsengumi in Kyoto
Chrysanthemum festival, Shinsaku meets at Shikokuya Inn
Chrysanthemum festival, Shinsaku meets at Shikokuya Inn
Shinsaku kills for the first time in raid at the Baishoin temple
Shinsengumi moves headquarters from Mibu to Nishi Honganji;
Sōzaburo and Tashiro Hyōzō join the corps
Keiō Era begins on this day
Tomiyama Yahei engages in personal fight, killing Sakura
Shikanai's child born, (does not line up with rest of timeline in the chp)
Okubo and Ito have a secret meeting at Ichiriki in Gion Hanamikoji cementing their alliance before Ito's departure from Shinsengumi

Abe Jūrō and Uchiumi Jūrō return from hunting to the Gessin-in. They were gone during the battle at Aburanokōji, and when they returny, they learn that their corps has been destroyed and most of their comrades slain. Abe and Uchiumi defect to the Satsuma army.
Official declaration of the Imperial Restoration. Tokugawa Yoshinobu, the last shogun, leaves Edo.
Middle of 1st month, Ohayashi Hyogo arrives at headquarters
Nakakura Shuzen discovered to have been attacked
Tainoshin agrees to leave Shinsengumi with the Itō faction

Tainoshin gets involved in a fight defending Suzuki Mikisaburō. The fallout from this minor scuffle kicks off a series of events which ends in the Goryo Eiji Incident, an intra-party split within the Shinsengumi
Tani Sanjūrō is defeated in combat
placard thrown into Kamo river with the notice board incident
26th day of 9th month Itō broaches the idea of splitting from the corps with Kondo
Takeda Kanryūsai's is executed by Saitō Hajime on a toll bridge over the Kamo River
Hirano Kazumi attacks Tomiyama Yahei by the Yugyō temple on Shichijo Avenue
Itō faction leaves for Choenji Temple
After several months of discussions, the Shogunate grants samurai status to members of the Shinsengumi
Itō faction (along with Tainoshin) moved to Gesshin-in Temple
Itō is assassinated at Aburanokoji
Battle of Toba-Fushimi, after which the Shinsengumi is driven out of Kyoto
